title: Left adjoints to Cartesian restrictions give cocartesian transport
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], Cartesian and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and coherent adjunctions of [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data]. All categories and mapping spaces fit in a fixed containing universe. Let $p:E\to B$ be a Cartesian fibration of quasicategories, with fibers $E_b$ and coherent restriction functors $f^*:E_c\to E_b$ for each edge $f:b\to c$ of $B$. Suppose every $f^*$ admits a left adjoint $L_f:E_b\to E_c$. Then $p$ is also a cocartesian fibration, and its covariant transport over $f$ is equivalent to $L_f$. More precisely, for any specified adjunction $L_f\dashv f^*$ with unit $\eta^f:\mathrm{id}_{E_b}\to f^*L_f$ and any $x\in E_b$, there is a $p$-cocartesian edge $u_x:x\to L_fx$ over $f$ whose image under the Cartesian mapping-space equivalence
$$\operatorname{hofib}_f\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_E(x,L_fx)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(b,c)\bigr)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{E_b}(x,f^*L_fx)$$
is $\eta^f_x$, up to its specified homotopy. Thus one may choose cocartesian lifts to correspond to the units of the given fiber adjunctions. No presentability or completeness hypothesis on the base or fibers is imposed.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 6.2.5.7 (02FP), implication (2) to (1), and the opposite of Proposition 6.2.5.4 (02FN), whose proof constructs lifts from the adjunction counit (dually, unit). Also Gepner-Haugseng arXiv:1312.3178 Lemma 3.6.6 uses this criterion. Read online; archival copy WANTED. These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Fix f:b→c, write R=f^* and L=L_f, and let i_b,i_c denote the fiber inclusions. The assumed coherent Cartesian restriction witness is h:Δ¹×E_c→E with endpoints i_b R and i_c, with Cartesian components r_y:Ry→y over f. For x∈E_b the unit η_x:x→RLx followed by r_{Lx}:RLx→Lx specifies an inner 2-horn in E. Its base is the degenerate triangle with successive edges id_b,f and long edge f. Since p is inner, fill this horn over that triangle and call its long edge u_x:x→Lx. Thus u_x lies exactly over f. The triangle and the Cartesian mapping-fiber equivalence for r_{Lx} identify u_x with η_x, with the chosen homotopy retained. Write H_a(v,z)=hofib_a(Map_E(v,z)→Map_B(pv,pz)) for the rest of the proof.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.5.4 (02FN), dualized unit construction; mapping-fiber formulation in 01TQ

proof.text: For y∈E_c, precomposition by u_x defines Map_{E_c}(Lx,y)→H_f(x,y). The Cartesian mapping-fiber equivalence for r_y identifies its target with Map_{E_b}(x,Ry). Under this identification the map sends v to R(v)∘η_x: indeed the coherent witness h gives v∘r_{Lx}≃r_y∘R(v), and the triangle in step 1 and associativity give v∘u_x≃r_y∘R(v)∘η_x. These are homotopies of mapping-space maps: naturality of h is supplied as a simplicial map on Δ¹×E_c, not merely as a pointwise equation. The adjunction mapping-equivalence node says exactly that v↦R(v)∘η_x is an equivalence, using the given coherent unit, counit and triangle homotopies. Consequently Map_{E_c}(Lx,y)→H_f(x,y) is an equivalence for every y.

Fix z∈E_d and a vertex g∈Map_B(c,d); choose a p-Cartesian lift e:y→z over g, so y∈E_c. Choose a composite a=gf and its 2-simplex in B. The Cartesian mapping criterion for e with test object x says Map_E(x,y)≃Map_E(x,z)×^h_{Map_B(b,d)}Map_B(b,c). Take the homotopy fiber over f of the projection to Map_B(b,c). Pasting homotopy pullbacks identifies H_f(x,y)≃H_a(x,z). The Cartesian mapping-fiber statement for e with test object Lx gives Map_{E_c}(Lx,y)≃H_g(Lx,z). Under these two equivalences the map H_g(Lx,z)→H_a(x,z) induced by precomposition with u_x is the map of step 2: the square has horizontal arrows precomposition by u_x and vertical arrows postcomposition by e, and commutes up to the associativity homotopy. Thus this map of homotopy fibers is an equivalence. All equivalences here use path pullbacks with their specified commutation homotopies. The inner mapping-fiber node makes the mapping projections Kan fibrations, so the constant-path comparison also permits the strict mapping fiber when needed; no strict fiber is silently substituted for a homotopy fiber.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.5.7 (02FP), global comparison in the proof of (2)⇒(1)

proof.text: Put S=Map_B(c,d), T=Map_B(b,d), Y=Map_E(x,z) and X=Map_E(Lx,z). Precomposition with f gives S→T, and precomposition with u_x gives X→Y, with the homotopy-commuting square induced by p. Its comparison is k:X→P=Y×^h_T S. All four mapping spaces and the path pullback P are Kan by the mapping-fibrancy and path-pullback statements. Regard k as a map of spaces over S; the base map is id_S, a weak equivalence. Homotopy-pullback pasting identifies the homotopy fiber of P→S over g with H_{gf}(x,z), while that of X→S is H_g(Lx,z). The induced map is precisely step 3's equivalence, with the path coordinates retained. Homotopy-fiber detection therefore makes k a weak equivalence. This holds for every z, including empty S. The cocartesian mapping criterion now says that u_x is p-cocartesian.

The map p is already an inner fibration. For every edge f:b→c and every source x∈E_b, steps 1–4 give a p-cocartesian edge u_x over f with target L_fx. Substitution into the definition makes p a cocartesian fibration. Step 1 supplies the specified-unit clause for any prescribed adjunction L_f⊣f^*.

source.place: Definition 2.4.2.1 and its cocartesian dual, as stated in def-coef-infinity-fibrations.

proof.text: To choose these edges coherently, take K=E_b in the fixed containing universe. Clause (1) of the edge-pullback mapping-fiber node states that p_K:Fun(K,E)→Fun(K,B) is an inner fibration. In Fun(K,E), the given coherent unit gives an edge i_b→i_bRL; restricting h along L gives an edge i_bRL→i_cL. Their images form the inner horn of the degenerate base triangle on the constant-diagram edge Δ_K f. Fill this horn using p_K. Its long edge is a map U:K×Δ¹→E, with endpoints i_b and i_cL and pU=f pr_{Δ¹}. Hence U factors degreewise through E_f. Evaluating the filled 2-simplex at each x gives precisely a triangle of the form in step 1. Choose the u_x by these evaluations; steps 2–4 apply to each of them and prove them cocartesian. Thus U witnesses the functor L itself as coherent covariant transport over f. No assertion that Fun(K,E_f)→Fun(K,E) is inner is required.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.5.7 (02FP) and coherent transport construction in 019M

proof.text: Let T:E_b→E_c be any other covariant transport with a coherent witness of cocartesian edges. Opposite simplicial sets exchange the outer horn indices, so the defining horn conditions make p^op:E^op→B^op Cartesian. Reverse the parameter Δ¹ in the witnesses U for L and the witness for T, and take opposites in the fiber variable. These are coherent Cartesian witnesses over f^op:c→b, with source endpoint i_c∘L^op (respectively i_c∘T^op) and target endpoint the inclusion i_b:E_b^op→E^op. Their common domain is E_b^op. The transport-uniqueness node applies to p^op and gives a natural equivalence L^op≃T^op in Fun(E_b^op,E_c^op). Taking opposites (and reversing the equivalence if necessary) gives L≃T in Fun(E_b,E_c). Together with the actual witness U from step 6 this proves the claimed equivalence with covariant transport.

Statement: matches Kerodon 02FP (Prop. 6.2.5.7, read online), direction (2)=>(1) plus the 'e_! left adjoint to e^*' clause. The base here is quasicategories, a special case of Kerodon's simplicial-set base. No hypothesis is added or dropped and the statement is not weakened; the item is not a target. Steps: (1) The inner horn (eta_x, r_{Lx}) over s_0(f) is filled to give u_x exactly over f; the Cartesian mapping-fiber node identifies u_x with eta_x. (2) The naturality square of h gives (u_x)^* ~ (r_y)_* o (v |-> R(v) eta_x); this is an equivalence by the adjunction mapping-equivalence node, whose triangle homotopies come from the 2-simplices of def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data. (3) For a Cartesian lift e over g, the Cartesian criterion plus pasting gives H_f(x,y) ~ H_{gf}(x,z), and the mapping-fiber node gives Map_{E_c}(Lx,y) ~ H_g(Lx,z); the square commutes by associativity. (4) Fiber detection is applied over id_S, so its weak-equivalence hypothesis holds; the cocartesian mapping criterion then makes u_x cocartesian. (5) The definition gives that p is a cocartesian fibration. (6) Clause (1) of the edge-pullback node (p_K is inner for K=E_b) gives a single coherent filler U. (7) Since p is cocartesian by step 5, p^op is Cartesian. The reversed witnesses U^op and T^op fit the hypotheses of lem-coef-infinity-transport-uniqueness exactly (b:=c, b':=b), so L ~ T.
